Individual requests may be possible for simple vegetable dishes but cross-contact with fish and meat should be assumed throughout.

chef_bio.background: Kataoka Keisuke opened the original Yuzen in Himeji in 2011, building a neighbourhood izakaya around Harima-region sake and locally sourced seafood. On April 15, 2024, a fire broke out on the second floor of the building housing the restaurant; the first-floor shop suffered extensive damage and could not reopen at that location. Rather than closing permanently, Kataoka rebuilt and reopened on September 1, 2024 as 遊膳 本店 (Main Store) in a new space on Miyuki-dori, roughly a three-minute walk from the original site.
chef_bio.philosophy: Hyper-local sourcing — seafood from daytime nets, lotus root from Hirohata district, Banshu jidori chicken — presented in a relaxed, counter-heavy izakaya that regulars describe as feeling unchanged despite the move.
chef_bio.specialty: Daily-changing sashimi featuring fish sourced same-day from local Himeji fisheries, paired with rare Harima-district sake such as Honda Shoten's 龍力 (Ryuriki) and Okubanshu labels

anecdotes.text: After the April 2024 fire destroyed the original space, Kataoka preserved the dark-brown colour scheme, the counter arrangement, and the shoe-removal entrance style at the new location, so returning guests would feel at home. Customers greeted him on reopening with 'Thank you for coming back,' and reservations filled daily.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Himeji Keizai Shimbun confirms owner Kataoka Keisuke, the 2011 founding, the April 15 2024 second-floor fire that damaged the ground-floor shop, and the September 1 2024 reopening as 本店 on Miyuki-dori (~3 min away, ~15 tsubo, counter 6 + sunken 4 tables/16 seats) with the dark-brown scheme, counter layout, and shoe-removal preserved and grateful returning customers. The Hirohata lotus root, Banshu jidori, and Ryuriki/Okubanshu sourcing details are from Tabelog and other listings.

gf_cross_contamination.text: No allergen menu or GF protocol is documented. Tempura is offered and the fryer's dedication is unknown, making cross-contamination from wheat batter a real risk.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Standard wheat-containing shoyu is used throughout; no tamari or GF soy sauce alternative has been mentioned in any source.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The kitchen handles seafood, chicken, and other animal proteins continuously; no plant-only prep area is documented.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No allergy-handling protocol or allergen chart has been reported. Phone reservations are available (079-287-8872) and would be the appropriate channel to discuss dietary needs before visiting.

positives.text: Menu is highly seasonal and made-to-order from daily-sourced local ingredients, which means the kitchen may be able to accommodate specific requests if contacted in advance.

cultural_comfort.note: A traditional Japanese izakaya with shoe-removal entry and tatami/sunken seating; menus are in Japanese, staff interaction is typical of a local neighbourhood pub with little expected English.

himeji_asian_dining_kingyoran.gf_detail: No gluten-free menu, labeling, or certification. The kitchen serves karaage (wheat-battered fried chicken), spring rolls with wrappers, soy-sauce-based marinades, and curry sauces whose gluten status is unknown. Wheat-containing soy sauce (shoyu) is almost certainly used. No dedicated fryer confirmed. Cross-contamination risk is unconfirmed but probable in a full-service kitchen of this type. Celiacs should contact the restaurant directly before visiting.
himeji_asian_dining_kingyoran.vegan_detail: No dedicated vegan menu or labeling. The kitchen uses fish-based broths (pho dashi), chicken, shrimp, and dairy across most dishes. A vegetable pho (五目フォー) appears on the menu and some salads could be meatless, but hidden animal ingredients — fish sauce, oyster sauce, egg — are standard in Southeast Asian cooking and not disclosed. Ask staff about specific dishes; vegan accommodation is not guaranteed.

chef_bio.background: Opened around 2009 in the Omizo-suji covered shopping arcade about a 6-minute walk north of Sanyo Himeji Station. It is said to have earlier operated as アジアンダイニング金魚 before rebranding to 金魚蘭. The kitchen describes its approach as 創作アジア料理 — creative Asian cooking drawing on Thai, Vietnamese, and Indonesian influences — using ingredients sourced directly from Southeast Asian countries.
chef_bio.philosophy: Dishes are calibrated to Japanese palates — spice levels are kept accessible — while the interior maintains a warm, wood-toned Southeast Asian atmosphere aimed at a largely female lunchtime crowd.
chef_bio.specialty: Daily-rotating lunch sets (本日のおすすめランチ, around ¥1,050) featuring a tray of small plates: fresh spring rolls, pho variants, multigrain rice with free refills, and a rotating dessert such as Vietnamese coffee custard or tropical fruit parfait.

anecdotes.text: A TripAdvisor reviewer who visited after Himeji Castle praised the service as 'awesome' and rated it among the city's top 30 restaurants out of more than 3,000.
A Japanese blog review noted the daily lunch set arrives on a large tray with five or more small dishes plus multigrain rice with free refills — unusually generous for the roughly ¥1,050 price point.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Gnavi confirms the Omizo-suji arcade location (~6 min from Sanyo Himeji Station), the 創作アジア料理 concept with imported Southeast-Asian ingredients, ~¥1,050 daily lunch sets (spring rolls, pho, multigrain rice with refills, dessert), and 45 seats. The 2009 opening year and the earlier '金魚' name could not be independently confirmed and are hedged.

gf_cross_contamination.text: No information available about cross-contamination controls. The kitchen fries karaage and spring rolls; a shared fryer is likely but unconfirmed.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: No gluten-free soy sauce (tamari) is mentioned anywhere. Standard wheat-containing shoyu is almost certainly used in marinades and sauces across the menu.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Fish sauce and oyster sauce are standard condiments in Thai and Vietnamese cooking; the kitchen does not label or disclose their use on any documented menu or listing.

staff_allergy_handling.text: TripAdvisor reviewers note staff are friendly and accommodating despite no English menu, but no allergy protocol or allergen sheet is documented on any platform.

positives.text: A vegetable pho (五目フォー) is a standing menu item, suggesting some plant-forward dishes exist alongside meat-heavy ones.

cultural_comfort.note: No English menu, but staff are described by visitors as friendly and helpful with photos on the menu making ordering manageable.

himeji_warabi_mochi_senmonten_k.gf_detail: The shop uses domestic hon-warabi-ko (bracken-root starch), which contains no wheat. Kinako and black sesame toppings are also naturally gluten-free. No soy sauce, dashi, or wheat-containing sauces appear in the core warabi mochi. However, no dedicated gluten-free certification or allergen sheet is published; cross-contamination risk in the small kitchen is unknown. The soft-serve ice cream component and WARABI-TA drink ingredients have not been confirmed. Celiacs should call ahead (079-284-1318) to verify the current production setup before visiting.
himeji_warabi_mochi_senmonten_k.vegan_detail: Plain warabi mochi with kinako (roasted soybean powder) or black sesame topping is plant-based — no animal products in the core preparation. However, the soft-serve ice cream topping and the WARABI-TA drink contain or may contain dairy; ingredients for these were not confirmed online. Vegans should ask to confirm the specific item before ordering. No hidden dashi in wagashi context.
himeji_warabi_mochi_senmonten_k.hours_raw: Mar–Oct 11:00–18:00 (Sat, Sun & holidays from 10:00); Nov–Feb 11:00–17:00 (Sat, Sun & holidays from 10:00). Irregular days off.
himeji_warabi_mochi_senmonten_k.notes: [Mom & Pop] Kadofuji is a genuine warabi-mochi specialty shop that opened on June 22, 2021, in the Honmachi shopping street at the foot of Himeji Castle. The founder ate warabi mochi all over Japan and, through trial and error, developed an original recipe using domestic real warabi-mochi flour. The signature product "Warabi Mochi Zeimi," created in collaboration with a Michelin-starred chef, is characterized by a wobbly, melting texture and rich kinako (roasted soybean flour) flavor. It has since expanded into a franchise of 12 shops nationwide.

chef_bio.background: 門藤は2021年6月22日、姫路城の麓の本町商店街にオープンした本わらび餅の専門店。 創業者は全国のわらび餅を食べ歩き、試行錯誤を重ねた末に国産の本わらび餅粉を使った独自レシピを開発した。 ミシュランシェフとタイアップして生まれた看板商品「わらび餅 ぜいみ」は、ぷるぷる・とろとろの食感と豊かなきなこの風味が特徴。 その後、全国12店舗に拡大するフランチャイズ展開を行っている。
chef_bio.philosophy: 四季に寄り添うわらび餅——春は花見菓子、夏は冷製、秋は茶菓子、冬は温かく。 国産本わらび粉にこだわり、独自の弾力とまろやかな口溶けを追求する。
chef_bio.specialty: わらび餅 ぜいみ（ふくゆたか大豆きなこ・黒ごま・深煎り）、わらび餅ドリンク「WARABI-TA」

anecdotes.text: TV番組「マツコの知らない世界」では、きな粉のスペシャリスト穴沢聖子が「ぜいみ ふくゆたか」を紹介し、佐賀県産の高級大豆ふくゆたかを使ったきな粉の味わいが取り上げられた。
店主は全国のわらび餅を食べ歩き、ミシュランシェフとタイアップして「ぜいみ」を完成させたと公式サイトで紹介されている。

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト（about）は2021年6月22日開業、ミシュランシェフとのタイアップによる「ぜいみ」、国産本わらび粉を裏付ける。まとめ記事はマツコの知らない世界での穴沢聖子による紹介と全国12店舗展開を記載。

gf_cross_contamination.text: No dedicated gluten-free certification or allergen sheet is published. The kitchen is very small (8 seats); cross-contamination risk is unconfirmed.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: No soy sauce or wheat-based sauce is used in traditional warabi mochi preparation. The core product (bracken starch + sugar + kinako/sesame) does not contain wheat.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Soft-serve ice cream is served alongside warabi mochi; dairy cross-contact is possible if equipment is shared. WARABI-TA drink ingredients unconfirmed.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No published allergen handling protocol found. Visitors with severe allergies should call 079-284-1318 before visiting.

positives.text: Uses domestic hon-warabi-ko (bracken-root starch) — a wheat-free, naturally gluten-absent base ingredient, confirmed by the shop's own materials.
Core wagashi preparation (warabi mochi + kinako/sesame) involves no animal broths, sauces, or hidden wheat ingredients typical of savory Japanese cooking.

cultural_comfort.note: A small specialty sweets counter near Himeji Castle with minimal English; pointing at items and self-service ordering is straightforward, but staff communication will be in Japanese.

himeji_kimura.gf_detail: Standard yakitori tare (glaze) is soy-sauce-based and contains wheat. Ponzu used in the signature ひねぽん typically contains soy sauce. No dedicated gluten-free protocol, no allergen labeling, and no reported GF accommodation. Celiac diners should treat this as high-risk and call ahead (079-282-3881).
himeji_kimura.vegan_detail: Entirely a chicken-focused yakitori counter. Every dish centers on chicken (grilled skewers, ひねぽん, raw tori-sashi, chicken offal stew). There are no plant-based mains. Side dishes like tofu and salad appear on the menu but are accompaniments, not a vegan meal. Ponzu-dressed dishes likely contain fish-derived dashi. Not suitable for vegans.

himeji_kimura.notes: [Mom & Pop] A second-generation mama-san counter shop tucked inside Himeji's Honmachi shopping arcade. Chiaki took over the yakitori-ya from her mother around 2010, unwilling to see it close, and has kept running it as a tight 8-seat counter ever since.

chef_bio.origin: Honmachi Shopping Arcade, Himeji; exact founding date unknown but the current owner is at least a second generation.
chef_bio.background: A second-generation mama-san counter shop tucked inside Himeji's Honmachi shopping arcade. 千秋ママ (Chiaki) took over the yakitori-ya from her mother around 2010 — she thought closing it 'would be a waste' — and has kept running it as a tight 8-seat counter ever since, working with fresh morning-delivered Tajima chicken.
chef_bio.philosophy: Keep old Himeji drinking-culture alive — affordable skewers from ¥130, quality aged chicken, and a no-frills counter where regulars return when they need somewhere familiar.
chef_bio.specialty: ひねぽん (hineppon) — sliced aged hen (ひね鶏, a mature bird prized for its chewy, deeply flavored meat) dressed in ponzu, a Banshu izakaya specialty; because the shop keeps it prepared ahead it arrives quickly. The bone-in aged-hen thigh (骨付ひね肉もも焼き), grilled to order, is another regular favorite.

anecdotes.text: A local blogger noted the hineppon comes out fast because the shop prepares it in advance — 'shops that grill it to order take longer' — a sign of how central the dish is to the menu.

Chiaki told a visiting blogger she took over the shop from her mother because 'closing it would be a waste,' and had been running it for about six years as of the 2016 article, placing the handover around 2010.
A solo-travel blogger staying at a nearby guesthouse described it as the ideal neighborhood counter for one — intimate, warm, and packed with salaryman regulars.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: himeji588（2016）は店主金井千秋（千秋ママ）、母からの約6年前の継承、8席、朝びき但馬鶏、130円～の串を裏付ける。ma8coroブログはひねぽんが仕込み済みで早く出ること、骨付ひね肉もも焼きを記載（『発祥』の記述はどの出典にもない）。

gf_cross_contamination.text: No information on cross-contamination controls. This is a small open counter grill; shared cooking surfaces are standard for yakitori-ya and no GF protocol has been documented anywhere.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Yakitori tare (the standard glaze applied to grilled skewers) is soy-sauce-based and contains wheat. The signature ひねぽん uses ponzu, which in Japan typically also contains soy sauce. Wheat exposure is likely on most non-shio (salt-only) items.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Every dish involves chicken or chicken-derived ingredients (offal stew, tori-sashi, yakitori). Any vegetable side dish shares prep space with raw chicken.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No allergy-handling protocol documented in any source. One reviewer noted a custom shio-only request was casually accommodated, suggesting flexibility, but this is not evidence of allergen-safe preparation.

positives.text: Salt-grilled (shio) skewers are available on request and can be prepared without tare glaze, potentially reducing (but not eliminating) soy sauce exposure for those with mild sensitivity.

cultural_comfort.note: A counter izakaya packed with regulars; no English signage or menu — Japanese-language navigation expected, though the warm mama-san atmosphere is welcoming to respectful visitors.

himeji_tonraishun.gf_detail: The Chinese noodles use wheat-containing noodles. Shumai wrappers are also made of wheat flour. The Worcestershire dipping sauce normally contains wheat as well. There is no gluten-free labeling or alternative menu whatsoever, and removing wheat is effectively impossible. Not accommodated for celiac disease or wheat allergy. Assessment: not celiac-safe.
himeji_tonraishun.vegan_detail: Almost every menu item uses animal ingredients. The Chinese-noodle broth is kombu- and iriko (dried sardine)-based, using seafood. The shumai contains pork. The Worcestershire dipping sauce may also contain animal ingredients. There is no note of vegan alternatives or accommodation. Assessment: not vegan-friendly.
himeji_tonraishun.notes: [Mom & Pop] Founded in 1946 (Showa 21) in postwar Himeji as an udon and fried-rice shop. During the era of food shortages, the practice of using scraps left over from cooking—such as pork fat trimmings and cabbage cores—without waste in staff meals is said to be the origin of its shumai. After repeated refinement, the current recipe was already complete when it relocated to its present location in Nishinikaimachi in 1952 (Showa 27). For nearly 80 years since its founding, this popular casual Chinese eatery—keeping its Showa-era interior and tableware largely intact—has been cherished by Himeji residents across generations.

chef_bio.background: 1946年（昭和21年）、終戦直後の姫路に創業した町中華食堂。 食糧難の時代、調理で出た豚肉の脂身やキャベツの芯などの端材を無駄なくまかないに使い始めたのがシュウマイの原型とされ、やがて客向けに改良されて看板メニューになった。 創業から70年以上、昭和の内装や食器をほぼそのままに、世代を超えて姫路市民に親しまれてきた。 現在は西二階町に店を構える。
chef_bio.philosophy: 変わらない味を守ること。 昭和の雰囲気を残したまま、素朴で飾らない大衆中華を提供し続けること。
chef_bio.specialty: 手作りシュウマイ（蒸し・焼き）と、昆布と煮干しベースの和風だしがきいた中華そば。 シュウマイは醤油ではなくウスターソースと練りがらしで食べるのが同店流。

anecdotes.text: シュウマイはもともと「まかない料理」として生まれた。創業当初、調理で余った豚肉の端材やキャベツの芯を捨てずに活用したのが始まりで、やがて客向けに改良されメニューに加わった。
ブロガーは外観を「銭湯みたい」と表現し、店内のレトロな食品サンプルや看板に「懐かしさに包まれまくり」と感想を残している。
テイクアウトのシュウマイは10・15・20個単位で購入可能。持ち帰り後は電子レンジより蒸し直し（約7分）が推奨されており、ふっくら仕上がると地元メディアが紹介している。

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: kochiki（創業70年）とgoguynetは昭和21年（1946）創業を裏付け、kochikiはまかない由来のシュウマイとソース＋からしで食べるスタイル、昆布・煮干しの中華そばを記載。1952年移転の具体的記述はどの出典にも確認できず削除。

gf_cross_contamination.text: グルテンフリー対応・コンタミネーション防止の取り組みについて公式・口コミいずれにも記載なし。小麦を大量に使う厨房環境と推定されるため、交差汚染リスクは高い。

soy_sauce_wheat.text: 中華そばのだしに醤油が使われているかは不明だが、一般的な中華そばには醤油（小麦含有）が使われる。シュウマイのタレはウスターソース（小麦含有）。醤油フリーの選択肢は確認できず。

vegan_cross_contact.text: 豚肉・魚介類を日常的に調理する厨房。ビーガン向けの分離調理や専用器具の対応は確認できず。

staff_allergy_handling.text: アレルギー・食事制限への対応について、公式サイト・口コミ・ブログいずれにも記載なし。

cultural_comfort.note: メニューは日本語のみ。英語対応の案内はなし。観光客も訪れるが、基本的に地元客向けの大衆食堂。

Those with celiac disease should inquire directly before visiting.
himeji_casa_isola_himeji_ekimae.vegan_detail: No vegan-specific menu or claims found. The kitchen centers on charcoal-grilled fish and seafood from Ieshima Island, pasta, and pizza. Hidden animal products (butter, cream, dashi, anchovies) are common in this style. Inquire in advance — no evidence of plant-based alternatives.

chef_bio.background: Murakado, who has ties to the fishing island of Ieshima, trained at Vermillion before opening Casa Isola independently in the Shikama district of Himeji (飾磨区清水) on July 30, 2020, in a former Chicken Heart storefront. After roughly six years there, the Shikama location closed on June 19, 2026, and the restaurant relocated to Minamicho (南町) in Himeji's station-front district, reopening on July 3, 2026, just 86m from Sanyo-Himeji Station.
chef_bio.philosophy: A hyper-local Italian izakaya that fuses Italian technique with the coastal flavors of Seto Inland Sea fishing islands.
chef_bio.specialty: Creative charcoal-grilled Italian using fresh seafood sourced from Ieshima Island — dishes such as charcoal-grilled fish and scallops, oil pasta with spicy cod roe, and fresh fish carpaccio sit alongside pizza and grilled meats.

anecdotes.text: The restaurant's name — Casa Isola, 'house of the island' — is a nod to the chef's roots on Ieshima (家島), an island off Himeji known for its fishing industry and seafood.
The Shikama original opened in July 2020 in a former Chicken Heart chain storefront, closed on 19 June 2026, and relocated to Minamicho near Himeji's main station, reopening 3 July 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: budou-chan（open-casaisola）はバーミリオン出身のシェフ、家島の海鮮を使う創作炭火イタリアン、2020/7/30飾磨開業、店名の意味を裏付ける。kaitenheitenは2026/6/19閉店・7/3南町移転を記載。TabelogとInstagram（@casa.isola＝村角徳昭）が新店の南町60-2・山陽姫路駅86m・7/3開業とシェフ名を裏付ける。

soy_sauce_wheat.text: No explicit soy sauce usage confirmed, but the restaurant blends Japanese and Italian flavors (e.g., ponzu-dressed chicken, fusion small plates), making shoyu — which contains wheat — a realistic ingredient in some dishes. No GF soy sauce alternative has been identified.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The kitchen handles fish, seafood, meat, cheese, and eggs as central ingredients. No separation for plant-based diners is indicated.

cultural_comfort.note: Small counter-heavy neighborhood Italian izakaya run by a single owner-chef; Japanese is the working language and non-Japanese guests should expect limited English.

himeji_shun_no_tenpura_to_kiset.gf_detail: Tempura is the signature dish — the batter is made with wheat flour, making this fundamentally unsafe for celiac diners. Soy sauce (containing wheat) is used in dipping sauces and for Himeji oden. No gluten-free menu, dedicated fryer, or allergy accommodation is mentioned on any source. The restaurant uses "Dr.Fry" advanced frying technology for texture/flavor purposes, not for dietary accommodation. Cross-contamination risk is high in a tempura kitchen.
himeji_shun_no_tenpura_to_kiset.vegan_detail: This is a tempura and seasonal Japanese cuisine restaurant with no vegan options identified. The tempura batter contains wheat flour and likely egg. Standard Japanese dashi (likely katsuobushi/bonito-based) is used in soups and sauces. Himeji oden is served with ginger soy sauce. Chawanmushi (savory custard) contains shrimp. Seafood is central to the menu. No vegan accommodations are mentioned on any platform.

chef_bio.background: Kichifuku opened on October 18, 2018, occupying the ground floor of the Daiwa Roynet Hotel Himeji in the station-front district. It is operated by Seiko Club (清交倶楽部), a Himeji-based company that also runs other local dining establishments including Miketide and Fukutei. The layout divides the space between a tatami and window-facing side overlooking National Route 2 and a counter side opening toward the Omizo-suji covered shopping arcade — enabling weather-protected pedestrian access from Himeji Station.
chef_bio.philosophy: The kitchen emphasizes seasonal rotation and local sourcing from the Harima region, pairing freshly fried tempura with about 15 carefully selected local sake from Harima breweries. The approach is convivial and unpretentious — combining the craftsmanship of a tempura counter with the relaxed atmosphere of a neighborhood izakaya.
chef_bio.specialty: Seasonal tempura featuring Harima-region ingredients, including conger eel (anago) — a Himeji specialty billed as 姫路名物穴子 — fried using 'Dr.Fry' technology, a commercial radio-wave molecular fryer said to sharply cut the coating's oil absorption. Counter seating lets diners watch each piece fried to order.

anecdotes.text: A reviewer on 4travel noted the tempura arriving crispy and hot, with the natural sweetness of the vegetables drawn out — and also called out the Himeji oden, a regional style served with ginger soy sauce, as a standout with well-absorbed flavors.
A local food blog documented the October 2018 opening, noting the restaurant's layout connects directly to the Omizo-suji covered arcade, giving shoppers dry-weather access from Himeji Station.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: budou-chanは2018/10/18開業、清交倶楽部運営（Miketide・福亭など）、ダイワロイネットホテル1階、国道2号側とみゆき通り側の造りを裏付ける。公式gorpとぐるなびは姫路名物穴子、播磨の地酒常時約15種、Dr.Fry（油の吸収を抑える調理機）を裏付ける。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Tempura is fried in shared fryers using wheat-flour batter as the core technique. Cross-contamination of any non-battered item with wheat flour is near-certain in a tempura kitchen. No source mentions any GF-safe fryer or protocol.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Himeji oden is served with ginger soy sauce. Tempura dipping sauce (tentsuyu) typically contains soy sauce and mirin. Standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat. No tamari or GF soy sauce alternative is mentioned anywhere.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The menu is built around seafood and dashi-based broths. Tempura batter likely contains egg. Miso soup accompaniments and chawanmushi (savory egg custard with shrimp) are standard menu items. No vegan-safe prep path is identifiable.

cultural_comfort.note: English menus are available, but the restaurant is a primarily Japanese-speaking establishment inside a business hotel; basic Japanese or pointing at the menu is sufficient for ordering.

himeji_yumeno_soba_otemae_ten.gf_detail: Soba noodles in Japan are almost always blended with wheat flour (typically 80/20 buckwheat-to-wheat, confirmed for this restaurant). Oden is served with ginger soy sauce, which contains wheat. No gluten-free options, dedicated fryer, or allergen accommodation information found. Cross-contamination risk is significant given the shared kitchen and standard Japanese soy sauce (shoyu) use throughout. This restaurant is not suitable for celiac diners.
himeji_yumeno_soba_otemae_ten.vegan_detail: The menu is built around fish cake (kamaboko) products from Yamasa Kamaboko — oden features sardine tsumire, shrimp rolls, chikuwa, and fishcake-based items throughout. Soba broth (tsuyu) is typically made with katsuobushi (bonito). There are no vegan options identified on the menu.

chef_bio.background: 夢乃蕎麦 大手前店 is a small soba and oden restaurant on the second floor of the Yamasa Kamaboko building near Himeji's Otemae-dori, directly operated by Yamasa Kamaboko Co., Ltd., a long-established Himeji fish-cake maker. The location brings the company's prized kamaboko to a sit-down table, pairing it with handmade soba made from Yumesakicho-grown buckwheat (a 2-to-8 blend) — a local variety from a town (夢前町) whose name literally reads 'dream-forward.' It is a ticketed, counter-style shop.
chef_bio.philosophy: Showcasing locally grown Yumesakicho buckwheat alongside Yamasa Kamaboko's fish-cake products in an unfussy counter setting at artisan-producer prices.
chef_bio.specialty: Himeji-style oden served with ginger soy sauce, and hand-made soba — which the shop encourages eating with salt to bring out the buckwheat's natural sweetness.

anecdotes.text: The soba can be ordered to eat with salt rather than tsuyu — a style the restaurant encourages to let the buckwheat's own sweetness come through, which surprises many first-time visitors.
One reviewer described the vegetable kakiage tempura as 'extraordinarily delicious' (とんでもなく美味しい) and left wishing she had also tried the oden, which she felt was better suited to autumn and winter.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelogとma8coroはヤマサ蒲鉾直営、大手前エリアの2階、券売機式カウンター、塩で食べる蕎麦、姫路おでん（生姜醤油）を裏付ける。公式yumenosoba.comは夢前町産そば粉の二八そばを裏付ける。

gf_cross_contamination.text: The soba noodles are an 80/20 buckwheat-wheat blend — wheat is a core ingredient, not a trace contaminant. The kitchen handles wheat extensively (tempura, soba, soy sauce-based oden broth). No separate preparation area or dedicated fryer for wheat-free cooking has been reported.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Oden is served with ginger soy sauce (生姜醤油), which contains wheat. The standard soba tsuyu dipping broth also contains soy sauce. Wheat is present throughout the menu via soy sauce and soba noodles.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Virtually every dish contains fish-derived ingredients: soba broth is katsuobushi-based, oden items are predominantly fishcake (kamaboko, chikuwa, tsumire), and the restaurant is operated by a fish cake manufacturer. No vegan-safe preparation is identifiable.

cultural_comfort.note: Ticket vending machine ordering at a compact counter-only room with casual Japanese service; no English signage or menus reported.

himeji_otemon_chaya.gf_detail: No gluten-free declarations. The menu features almond toast and stone-oven pancakes (both wheat-based) as signature items, as well as packaged sandwiches from the Yamazaki Shop. Warabi mochi (pure warabi starch) is traditionally gluten-free but no dedicated GF preparation is claimed and cross-contamination risk is unconfirmed. Beverages (coffee, tea, juices, ciders) are likely wheat-free but no allergen information is published. Do not assume safety without direct staff confirmation. Note: despite the Tabelog classification as そば, no soba or udon dishes appear on the actual current menu.
himeji_otemon_chaya.vegan_detail: No declared vegan menu. Warabi mochi (bracken-starch jelly) and most cold drinks are likely vegan by ingredients, but there are no allergen declarations. Almond toast uses butter; pancakes likely contain dairy and egg. The Yamazaki convenience shop section sells onigiri and sandwiches — ingredient labeling on packaged items may be checked in-store.

chef_bio.background: 大手門茶屋 is a public rest house operated by the 一般財団法人姫路市まちづくり振興機構 (Himeji City Urban Development Foundation), a civic body that manages tourism and urban facilities around the World Heritage castle grounds. It sits inside the Otemon (main gate) parking lot at 本町68, directly facing Himeji Castle, and serves as a refreshment stop for castle visitors.
chef_bio.philosophy: A city-run rest house prioritizing accessibility and convenience for castle tourists, offering light refreshments, original Himeji Castle merchandise, and free wheelchair rentals to welcome visitors of all abilities.
chef_bio.specialty: Almond toast (アーモンドトースト, ¥458) — thick-cut bread with butter and chopped almonds — alongside cafe drinks such as coffee and cappuccino, rice-koji amazake (米糀の甘酒), and a small Yamazaki convenience corner with bread, sandwiches and onigiri.

anecdotes.text: As a city-run rest house it lends wheelchairs free of charge and sells original Himeji Castle merchandise — from tote bags and smartphone stands to a Lego Architecture Himeji Castle set — reflecting its role as a managed public facility rather than a private business.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式（machishin）はまちづくり振興機構運営、大手門駐車場内・本町68、喫茶（コーヒー・カプチーノ等）、山崎コンビニコーナー、車椅子無料貸出、姫路城グッズを裏付ける。姫路観光ナビはアーモンドトースト458円・米糀の甘酒356円を記載。

cultural_comfort.note: A tourist-facing rest house at the Himeji Castle entrance serving an international visitor audience; signage and service are accessible to non-Japanese speakers.

himeji_himeyama_saryo.gf_detail: Kaiseki cuisine has many simmered dishes and sauces using soy sauce (contains wheat), and battered dishes such as tempura are also served (there is a note of "with salt only," but not for all items). No gluten-free accommodation is indicated. Presence of a dedicated fryer is unknown. Those with wheat allergy or celiac disease must inquire directly when reserving. Assessment: not celiac-safe.
himeji_himeyama_saryo.vegan_detail: The standard kaiseki course includes sashimi, grilled fish, beef dishes, and more, and plant-based-only accommodation has not been confirmed. The dashi is presumed bonito-flake/kombu-based but not officially stated. Because there is a note of "consult us for a healthy menu," inquiry is advised. No vegan accommodation is indicated. Assessment: not reliably vegan.
himeji_himeyama_saryo.hours_raw: Mon–Tue, Thu–Sun & holidays: lunch 11:30–14:00 (LO 13:00), dinner 17:00–21:30 (LO 20:00). Closed Wed, plus irregular days off.
himeji_himeyama_saryo.notes: The owner discovered a building converted from a traditional house over 100 years old (said to be a former sake brewery), fell in love with the charm of the space, and opened the restaurant. The building stands along the wall of Himeji Castle, in a quiet corner northwest of the castle.

chef_bio.origin: 兵庫県姫路市小利木町
chef_bio.background: 築100年以上の古民家（元酒蔵とも伝わる）を改装した建物を発見したオーナーが、その空間の魅力に惚れ込み店を開いた。 建物は姫路城の城壁沿い、姫路城北西の閑静な一角に佇む。
chef_bio.philosophy: 「自分がおいしいと思うものをお客様にも楽しんでいただけたら」——既製品を一切使わず、近隣の信頼する鮮魚店・青果店から仕入れた旬の素材を最大限に活かす手間ひまを惜しまない料理作り。
chef_bio.specialty: 大名つづら（10種以上の季節料理＋抹茶フォンデュのセット御膳）および抹茶フォンデュ

anecdotes.text: 署名デザートの抹茶フォンデュのソースは、オーナーの奥様が試行錯誤を重ねて完成させたもの。SNSで話題となり学生から大人まで幅広い層に人気が広がった。
店内には水引アートや繊細なバラン細工が飾られており、そのうちの一つは姫路城を模して作られている。オーナーが技術を磨いた手仕事の片鱗が随所に見られる。
看板メニュー「大名つづら」の中身は仕入れた食材によって毎日変わる。胡麻豆腐は手作りで、そのままでもたれ不要と評判。

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: local-primeはオーナー兼料理長・博多勝也、築100年以上の古民家、城壁沿い北西の立地、大名つづら（10種以上＋抹茶フォンデュ）、奥様が完成させた抹茶ソース、姫路城を模した水引・バラン細工を裏付ける。tanosuは大名つづらが日替わり、手作り胡麻豆腐を裏付ける。

gf_cross_contamination.text: 天ぷら・油物メニューあり（「塩のみで」との記述はあるが専用フライヤーの使用有無は未確認）。小麦を含む揚げ物と同一厨房・フライヤーを共有している可能性がある。

soy_sauce_wheat.text: 懐石料理の標準的な調理で醤油（小麦含有）が煮物・タレ・だし等に使用されると推定される。グルテンフリー醤油（タマリ等）使用の明示なし。

vegan_cross_contact.text: 刺身・牛肉・焼き魚・海老天ぷらなど動物性食材を同一厨房で扱うため、植物性料理との接触リスクがある。ビーガン専用調理設備の記述なし。

staff_allergy_handling.text: 「ヘルシーメニューご相談」との表記あり（ぐるなびページ）。完全予約制のため、予約時に食物アレルギー・食事制限を事前相談できる環境にある。ただしアレルギー対応の専門的な体制や認証の記載はなし。

positives.text: 完全予約制で少人数制のため、事前に食の制限を伝える余地がある。オーナーが素材を個別に選んでいる小規模独立店であり、融通が利きやすい可能性がある。

cultural_comfort.note: 完全予約制の懐石料理店。英語メニューあり（訪日外国人向け対応）。靴を脱いで入店する畳座敷あり。カード決済可能で外国人対応の準備はあるが、基本的に日本語のやり取りが中心。

himeji_ramen_masamasa.gf_detail: Wheat is central to every dish: house-made wheat noodles are the signature, and the shoyu tare is made with conventional wheat-containing soy sauce. No gluten-free noodle or tamari alternative is mentioned anywhere. Cross-contamination from noodle production in-house is near-certain.
himeji_ramen_masamasa.vegan_detail: All menu items contain meat or fish. The shoyu ramen uses chicken-based broth with chicken oil; the niboshi ramen is built on dried sardine dashi; mazesoba features braised pork; even the tsukemen dipping broth is animal-based. No plant-based alternatives are offered.

chef_bio.origin: Himeji, Hyogo Prefecture (relocated from earlier Himeji location)
chef_bio.background: Owner Hiramatsu was born in Kanagawa but grew up in Himeji, which he considers his hometown. He spent 16 years as a corporate manager before making the leap to ramen — a decision that took about six months of persuading his family. He opened the original shop, 麺昌まさ (Menshow Masa), on November 4, 2015, and relocated and rebranded it as Ramen Masamasa on December 23, 2023.
chef_bio.philosophy: Hiramatsu describes his ideal as ramen 'where diners recall the ingredients and the producers behind them.' Self-taught rather than formally apprenticed, he favors clear, delicate broths over milky ones, and works with specialty flour, hand-selected soy sauce, jidori local-chicken stock, and niboshi (dried sardine) as a primary aromatic.
chef_bio.specialty: Shoyu ramen with aromatic chicken oil and a deeply layered soy-sauce broth; award-winning kombu-water tsukemen

anecdotes.text: Hiramatsu describes himself as 'someone who obsesses over details and constantly seeks knowledge' — a self-description that echoes his 16-year corporate career as a manager before pivoting entirely to ramen.
The kombu-water tsukemen took top honors in the tsukemen category of Pia's Ultimate Ramen Kansai rankings, and the shoyu ramen earned a Runner-Up Grand Prix in the 2025 Kansai edition.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: krkjapan（2022）は神奈川生まれ・姫路育ち、16年の会社員（管理職）、約半年の家族説得、2015/11/4開業、素材と作り手を思い出せるラーメン、煮干し・地鶏を裏付ける。Tabelogは2023/12/23の移転・改名、昆布水つけ麺と至高のラーメン関西での受賞・2025準グランプリを記載。

gf_cross_contamination.text: House-made wheat noodles are produced on-site; wheat flour is in active use throughout service. Cross-contamination for anyone with celiac disease or serious wheat allergy is effectively unavoidable.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The shoyu tare uses conventional wheat-containing soy sauce selected by the owner for its aroma profile. No tamari or gluten-free soy sauce alternative is mentioned.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Chicken oil (鶏油) is used in the shoyu ramen broth, niboshi (dried sardine) is a core aromatic in the niboshi ramen, and braised pork features in the mazesoba. Animal products are present in every menu item with no plant-based alternative available.

positives.text: The owner's background as a detail-obsessed craftsman and his practice of hand-selecting premium ingredients suggest consistent, careful preparation — though no specific allergy protocol has been documented.

cultural_comfort.note: Counter-heavy lunch-only ramen shop with no English signage or menus noted; ordering is straightforward at the counter but expect Japanese only.

himeji_oden_to_kushikatsu_himej.gf_detail: Kushikatsu (the restaurant's core offering alongside oden) are deep-fried in wheat-based batter — wheat is central to the menu. The oden broth is made from konbu and katsuo (bonito) dashi. Standard Japanese soy sauce (which contains wheat) is used in the ginger soy sauce condiment. No gluten-free options, dedicated fryer, or allergen accommodation information appears anywhere on the restaurant's own pages or third-party listings. Celiac diners should avoid.
himeji_oden_to_kushikatsu_himej.vegan_detail: The oden broth is explicitly described as konbu and katsuo (bonito fish) dashi. Kushikatsu typically includes pork and other meats. The menu features sashimi, grilled chicken (hinepon), beef tendon, and egg dishes. No plant-based or vegan options are indicated anywhere on the menu or in any source. Hidden animal-derived dashi is present throughout.
himeji_oden_to_kushikatsu_himej.hours_raw: 11:00–23:15 daily (food L.O. 22:30, drinks L.O. 22:45); closed January 1 only
himeji_oden_to_kushikatsu_himej.notes: Operated by 株式会社otto, this restaurant occupies a stall inside 姫路のれん街 (Himeji Noren Street), a retro-style covered arcade of izakaya-format eateries on the ground floor of the Shin Festa Building, a one-minute walk from Himeji Station. The noren-gai concept evokes the atmosphere o

chef_bio.background: Operated by 株式会社otto, this restaurant occupies a stall inside 姫路のれん街 (Himeji Noren Street), a retro-style covered arcade of izakaya-format eateries on the ground floor of the Shin Festa Building (駅前363-1), about a one-minute walk from Himeji Station. The noren-gai concept evokes the atmosphere of a Showa-era alley of red-lantern drinking establishments.
chef_bio.specialty: Himeji oden — slow-simmered dashi, served from ¥176 with the city's signature house-made ginger soy sauce dipping condiment. The restaurant also serves kushikatsu (deep-fried skewers) from ¥132, including novelty items such as konnyaku shaped like Himeji Castle.

anecdotes.text: The konnyaku (devil's tongue jelly) in the oden is molded in the shape of Himeji Castle, a whimsical nod to the city's most famous landmark.

The restaurant leans into Himeji local specialties such as chanpon-yaki (a soba-and-udon mix that has been featured on TV), bokkake (beef offal simmered with konnyaku in a sweet-spicy sauce) and hineppon.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: otto2008.com（自社サイト）は本店を株式会社otto運営と裏付ける。ホットペッパーは姫路のれん街・シンフェスタビル・駅前徒歩1分、姫路おでん176円～（自家製生姜醤油）、串カツ132円～を記載。tanosuはお城の形のこんにゃくとぼっかけを裏付ける。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Kushikatsu (deep-fried battered skewers) is one of the two core menu categories. Wheat batter is in heavy use throughout service. No dedicated gluten-free fryer is mentioned anywhere.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The ginger soy sauce condiment (生姜醤油) served with oden is standard Japanese shoyu, which contains wheat. No tamari or gluten-free soy sauce alternative is mentioned.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The oden broth is made from konbu and katsuo (bonito fish) dashi. All oden ingredients simmer in this shared broth, making plant-based isolation impossible even for nominally vegetable items.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No allergy handling protocols, allergen menus, or dietary accommodation procedures are published on any platform. The restaurant's own site, Tabelog, HotPepper, Gurunavi, and Hitosara all lack allergen information.

cultural_comfort.note: Casual Showa-era izakaya atmosphere inside Himeji Noren Street; staff are noted as bright and welcoming but menus and service are in Japanese with no confirmed English-language support.

himeji_uomachi_matsubishi.gf_detail: Standard Japanese kaiseki relies heavily on wheat-based soy sauce (koikuchi shoyu) in sauces, marinades, and dipping preparations, and dashi stocks may be combined with soy sauce. Fried dishes (e.g. scorpionfish karaage noted in reviews) use wheat batter. No dedicated gluten-free menu, no tamari substitution, and no allergen information is published. Celiac diners should call ahead; safe options cannot be assumed without direct confirmation from the kitchen.
himeji_uomachi_matsubishi.vegan_detail: This is a traditional kaiseki and kappo restaurant built around Seto Inland Sea seafood — dishes regularly include katsuo/bonito dashi, fish-based broths, shellfish, whale hot pot, and sashimi. There is no stated vegan menu and no indication that plant-based courses are available. A diner with vegan requirements should contact the restaurant well in advance to discuss options, though a fully vegan kaiseki course would be very difficult here.
himeji_uomachi_matsubishi.hours_raw: Mon–Sat, pre-holidays & post-holidays 17:30–22:00 (L.O. 21:30), closed Sun & holidays
himeji_uomachi_matsubishi.notes: [Mom & Pop] An established kappo and kaiseki restaurant in Himeji's Uomachi district, in operation for multiple decades based on its multi-floor building and retro-era décor described by visitors as evocative of Japan's bubble period. The ground floor features counter seating; an upper floor

chef_bio.background: A well-established kappo and kaiseki restaurant in Himeji's Uomachi district. Its multi-floor building and retro décor — described by visitors as evocative of Japan's bubble period — suggest a long history. The ground floor features counter seating; an upper floor houses a whisky bar.
chef_bio.philosophy: A commitment to showcasing the natural flavors of carefully sourced local fish; the menu changes with the seasons and emphasizes the depth of ingredient quality over elaborate technique.
chef_bio.specialty: Seasonal Seto Inland Sea fish and shellfish — an extensive selection of small-plate (ippin) dishes anchored by premium seafood; winter specialties include fugu sashimi (tessa) and nabe courses featuring oysters, conger eel, duck, and seasonal seafood.

anecdotes.text: A visiting food blogger noted that the rice porridge (zosui) at the close of the hot-pot course was finished with nori and chives rather than the more common green onion — a small but memorable personal touch.
The same blogger observed that fugu, normally a signature item, was unavailable on their visit due to rising market prices — illustrating how closely the menu tracks seasonal and market conditions.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: hitosaraは日本料理・懐石/会席、上階のウイスキーバー、瀬戸内の魚、冬のふぐ（てっさ）・牡蠣・穴子・鴨の鍋を裏付ける。創業年数（『数十年』）や『100品以上』の具体は出典で確認できず、それぞれ緩めた。

gf_cross_contamination.text: No published information on cross-contamination controls. Fried items (scorpionfish karaage) appear on menus, indicating shared frying oil with wheat-battered foods is possible.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Traditional kappo cooking uses wheat-containing soy sauce throughout — in dipping sauces, simmered dishes, and marinades. No tamari or gluten-free soy sauce alternative is mentioned anywhere in available sources.

vegan_cross_contact.text: All courses are built around fish and seafood; bonito/katsuo dashi is standard in Japanese kappo cooking. No vegan-safe preparation lines are indicated.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No information on allergy handling procedures is publicly available. Diners with celiac disease or serious allergies should call the restaurant directly (079-288-0878) well before visiting.

cultural_comfort.note: Traditional upscale kappo setting aimed at business entertaining; staff dress formally and the atmosphere is refined — some comfort with Japanese dining customs is helpful, though no English-language service is indicated.

himeji_obanzai_to_jizake_yusai.gf_detail: Across obanzai and washoku in general, soy sauce (contains wheat), mirin, and dashi-shoyu are routinely used. Items using wheat flour, such as spring rolls, have been confirmed. No gluten-free accommodation is indicated. Presence of a dedicated fryer is unknown. Celiacs must confirm details by phone before visiting. Assessment: not celiac-safe.
himeji_obanzai_to_jizake_yusai.vegan_detail: The daily obanzai centers on seasonal vegetables and offers a solid range of vegetable dishes, but items using bonito dashi, chicken, and seafood are mixed in. Animal-based items such as "Himeji oden," "sake-steamed clams," and "fresh sashimi" are part of regular service. No plant-based-only course or explicit vegan menu could be confirmed. Confirm before visiting. Assessment: not reliably vegan.
himeji_obanzai_to_jizake_yusai.hours_raw: Tue–Fri 17:00–23:00 (LO 22:30), Sat, Sun & holidays 15:00–23:00 (LO 22:30). Note: on Sat, Sun & holidays 15:00–17:00 only obanzai is served. Closed Mon (or the following Tue if Mon is a holiday).
himeji_obanzai_to_jizake_yusai.notes: [Mom & Pop] Opened September 1, 2025, in Kubomachi, Himeji. A small dining spot on the 1st floor of the MISTRAL Kubomachi Building, a 5-minute walk from Sanyo Himeji Station.

chef_bio.background: 2025年9月1日に姫路市久保町にオープン。 山陽姫路駅から徒歩約5分、MISTRAL久保町ビル1階に構える小さな小料理屋。
chef_bio.philosophy: 「美味しく、楽しく、健康に。」をコンセプトに、管理栄養士の資格を持つ女将が栄養を考えた日替わりおばんざいと一品料理を提供。 地元・播磨の地酒を常時10種類以上厳選して揃える。
chef_bio.specialty: 日替わりおばんざい（季節野菜の家庭料理）と播磨の地酒

anecdotes.text: オーナーは管理栄養士の資格保有者で、健康面を考慮しながら季節の食材を使った日替わりメニューを毎日手作りしている。
ブログレポートによると、開店直後から常連客が多く訪れ、予約が取りにくい状況が続いているとの記述があった。

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelogは2025/9/1開業、久保町MISTRALビル1階、山陽姫路駅徒歩約5分、管理栄養士の女将、常時10種類以上の播磨地酒を裏付ける。ホットペッパーは採れたて野菜の健康的な日替わりおばんざいを裏付ける。

gf_cross_contamination.text: 春巻きなど小麦粉使用メニューが通常ラインナップに含まれており、調理場での交差汚染リスクを排除できない。

soy_sauce_wheat.text: 和食・おばんざいの調理では一般的な醤油（小麦含有）が使用されると考えられる。グルテンフリー醤油使用の明示はない。

vegan_cross_contact.text: かつお出汁・魚介・鶏肉を使うメニューが同じ厨房で調理される。植物性のみへの対応について明記なし。

staff_allergy_handling.text: オーナーが管理栄養士の資格を持つため、アレルギーへの理解は期待できるが、公式にアレルギー対応を謳った記述は確認されていない。来店前に電話（070-2352-3200）での事前確認を推奨。

positives.text: オーナーは管理栄養士の資格保持者で、健康を意識した季節野菜中心のおばんざいを提供しており、野菜メニューの種類が多い。

cultural_comfort.note: 小さなカウンター中心の小料理屋。英語メニューや英語対応スタッフの情報なし。日本語でのやり取りが基本。

himeji_kissa_fukunaga.gf_detail: No gluten-free options or allergy information documented anywhere across multiple sources. The signature black beef curry (developed with 30+ spices) likely contains wheat-based soy sauce; pasta is a core menu item; canelé contains wheat flour. Wheat is pervasive throughout the kitchen. No dedicated fryer information available. Celiacs should ask before ordering and be prepared that safe options may be very limited.
himeji_kissa_fukunaga.vegan_detail: No vegan-specific options documented. The menu centres on beef curry (3-day braised brisket), egg sandwiches with dashi-rolled egg, pasta, and dairy-heavy desserts (Italian pudding, canelé, cream sodas). Hidden dashi and dairy are very likely throughout. Visitors should ask staff, but vegan options appear very limited if available at all.
himeji_kissa_fukunaga.notes: [Mom & Pop] Opened on April 15, 2022 in the Kamihata Building directly adjacent to the Bon Marché Himeji shopping arcade, one minute on foot from Sanyo-Himeji Station. The café is operated by the Usagi Group (食菜家うさぎ), a Himeji-based dining company that runs several izakaya-style restaurants

chef_bio.background: Opened on April 15, 2022 on the 2nd floor of the Kamihata Building (南町9) adjacent to the Bon Marché Himeji shopping arcade, about one minute on foot from Sanyo-Himeji Station. The café is operated by the owner of the Usagi Group (食菜家うさぎ), a Himeji-based dining company that runs several izakaya-style restaurants in the area; a rabbit mascot ties the two together. It is a jazz-playing, retro-modern kissaten.
chef_bio.philosophy: The Usagi Group owner personally researched curries across Japan before collaborating with the kitchen team to develop the menu, aiming to pair serious, craft-level cooking with the relaxed, nostalgic atmosphere of a classic kissaten.
chef_bio.specialty: 自家製黒ビーフカレー (homemade black beef curry) — developed over about a year and a half using a spice blend (reported at around 30 spices) and a three-day preparation in which the beef is braised until it can be cut without teeth, then rested; colourful cream sodas (five colours — green, blue, red, yellow, purple) are the other signature draw, the melon-and-vanilla Fukunaga Green reportedly selling around 70 cups a day.

anecdotes.text: The signature black beef curry took roughly a year and a half to perfect, the owner travelling the country studying curry before settling on a spice blend (reported at around 30) and a three-day preparation for the beef.
The Fukunaga Green cream soda — a melon-and-vanilla drink with a striking emerald colour — became a hit, reportedly selling around 70 cups per day.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: tanosu・local-prime・budou-chan・公式(うさぎ)より。2022年4月15日、山陽姫路駅前カミハタビル2Fに開業。食菜家うさぎのオーナーが全国のカレーを研究して開発した自家製黒ビーフカレー(仕込み3日)と、5色のクリームソーダが名物。フクナガグリーン(メロン+バニラ)は1日約70杯。スパイス数は媒体により約30種/8〜9種と記述が分かれる。

soy_sauce_wheat.text: No allergen or soy sauce information published. The curry, pasta, and egg sandwich are all likely to involve wheat-based soy sauce or wheat-containing ingredients; no source confirms tamari or GF substitutes are available.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Dairy and eggs are core ingredients across the menu (Italian pudding, canelé, egg sandwich, cream sodas). No vegan cross-contact protocols documented.

cultural_comfort.note: Retro kissaten atmosphere with jazz; menus and signage are in Japanese only, but the relaxed café setting and solo-diner-friendly layout make it approachable for non-Japanese visitors who can point to menu items.

himeji_aprire.gf_detail: Standard Italian restaurant serving pizza and pasta, both of which are wheat-based. No gluten-free pasta or pizza alternatives are mentioned on any source. Bread (baguette) is a standard starter. No dedicated fryer information available. Wheat cross-contamination is a realistic concern in any standard Italian kitchen. Celiacs should call ahead (079-222-5511) to ask about gluten-free accommodation; currently no evidence supports safe dining for celiac without direct confirmation.
himeji_aprire.vegan_detail: Standard Italian menu centered on meat, fish, pasta, and pizza. No vegan or vegetarian labelling found on any source. Dishes include prosciutto, seafood pasta (sea urchin cream, carpaccio), and egg-topped preparations. Dairy (butter, cream, cheese) is prevalent throughout. Vegans should call ahead — Italian technique here relies heavily on animal products and hidden ingredients such as parsley-basil butter on bread service and cream-based sauces.
himeji_aprire.notes: Aprire is a multi-floor Italian restaurant tucked into a quiet residential-commercial block in Himeji's Jusshoshomacho district, a short walk south of Himeji Castle and roughly five minutes from Sanyo-Himeji Station. Despite its unassuming, somewhat hidden location on a low-traff

chef_bio.background: Aprire is a house-style Italian restaurant tucked into a quiet residential-commercial block in Himeji's Jūnishomaecho (十二所前町), roughly 200 metres (about three minutes' walk) from Sanyo-Himeji Station and a short walk from Himeji Castle. Despite its unassuming, hidden-gem location on a low-traffic street, it has built a loyal following of regulars who tend to fill the counter, and it runs as a small, personal operation.
chef_bio.philosophy: No explicit philosophy statement is published; the restaurant's reputation rests on seasonal ingredients, consistent quality, and attentive hospitality — staff have been noted holding food for returning guests as a gesture of care.
chef_bio.specialty: Seasonal Italian cooking — pasta and rich cream sauces, squid-ink risotto, wood-fired thin-crust pizza, carpaccio, and seasonal plates such as white-asparagus sauté with a fried egg and prosciutto with ripe melon; the house-made basil butter served with baguette is a recurring standout in guest accounts.

anecdotes.text: A blogger noted that despite minimal weekday foot traffic on the quiet backstreets around the restaurant, Aprire draws a steady crowd of regulars — 'a comfortable, welcoming establishment' even on slow evenings.
One guest recounted that staff set aside the remainder of their basil-butter dish so they could enjoy it again on a return visit the next day, illustrating the restaurant's attentiveness.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ・ma8coroブログ・Rettyより。姫路市十二所前町、山陽姫路駅から約200m(徒歩約3分)の一軒家イタリアン(隠れ家)。常連が多くカウンターが賑わう。イカ墨リゾット、生パスタ、薪窯ピザ、カルパッチョ、白アスパラのソテー、生ハムメロンなど。自家製バジルバターとバゲットが好評。オーナーシェフ名は非公表。

gf_cross_contamination.text: No dedicated gluten-free preparation area or protocols mentioned in any source; standard Italian kitchen with pasta, pizza, and bread service means wheat cross-contamination is a realistic concern.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: No soy sauce identified in sourced menu descriptions; cuisine is Italian, but wheat is present throughout via pasta, pizza dough, and bread. No gluten-free alternatives noted anywhere.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Dairy (butter, cream, cheese) and meat products are core to the menu. Basil butter is served as a standard bread accompaniment. No vegan-safe preparation protocols mentioned.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No allergy handling protocols or allergen menu documented in any fetched source. Direct phone contact (079-222-5511) is the only confirmed path to obtain allergy accommodation information.

positives.text: Small independent restaurant with a close-knit team (reportedly one owner, one chef), which may allow flexible accommodation requests if arranged in advance by phone.

cultural_comfort.note: A long-established local Italian spot with a loyal regular crowd; staff are attentive and hospitable, but the menu and communication are in Japanese with no English-language materials noted.

himeji_karaage_shu.gf_detail: Standard Japanese karaage batter contains wheat flour, and the marinade almost certainly uses conventional soy sauce (which contains wheat). No gluten-free options are listed anywhere online, no dedicated fryer information is available, and the shop has published no allergen information. Anyone with celiac disease should not assume safety without directly confirming ingredients and fryer practices with staff before ordering.
himeji_karaage_shu.vegan_detail: This is a dedicated chicken karaage shop — every menu item is meat-based (fried chicken, croquettes, fried takoyaki). There are no vegan options and no plant-based dishes on the menu.
himeji_karaage_shu.notes: [Mom & Pop] からあげ 秀 opened in March 2023 inside the いの屋敷 complex (also known as 家老屋敷A棟) at Himeji's Honmachi 68 — a historic-district shopfront at the entrance to the Karoyashiki ruins park on the main approach road to Himeji Castle.

chef_bio.background: からあげ 秀 opened on March 25, 2023 inside the いの屋敷 complex (also listed as 家老屋敷A棟1号) at Himeji's Honmachi 68 — a historic-district shopfront directly across from the Karoyashiki-ato park on the main approach to Himeji Castle.
chef_bio.specialty: 国産からあげ — freshly fried domestic chicken (Banshu-raised free-range bird) in a mixed breast-and-thigh portion, served in about five minutes from order. A signature side is the まるごとオレンジジュース, fresh juice served inside a hollowed-out whole orange.

anecdotes.text: Reviewers describe it as a hidden-gem rest stop for castle visitors, valued as much for its whole-orange juice as its fried chicken. An optional 本気(マジ)スパイス (serious spice blend) can be requested for heat.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ・budou-chan・ヒトサラ・家老屋敷跡公園利用者組合サイトより。2023年3月25日、姫路市本町68『いの屋敷/家老屋敷A棟1号』に開業。播州地鶏の国産からあげ(むね+もも、揚げたて約5分)と、まるごとオレンジジュースが名物。本気スパイス選択可。店主名は非公表。

gf_cross_contamination.text: No information is available about fryer sharing between different menu items (chicken, croquettes, fried takoyaki). Cross-contamination risk cannot be ruled out.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The karaage marinade almost certainly uses conventional Japanese soy sauce, which contains wheat. The batter is standard wheat-flour coating. Neither the shop nor any third-party source has published allergen or ingredient details.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The entire menu is meat-based; there is no plant-based cooking context here and cross-contact is not a relevant concern given no vegan items exist.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No information on staff allergy awareness or handling procedures is available from any source reviewed. Direct contact is required: 080-9014-9354.

cultural_comfort.note: A small local stall near Himeji Castle aimed primarily at Japanese tourists and locals; English menus or English-speaking staff are not confirmed, but simple counter ordering with pointing at menu boards is manageable.

himeji_takeda_no_anago_meshi_ma.gf_detail: The tare (sauce) and cooking liquid are made with standard Japanese soy sauce, which contains wheat. The rice is cooked in anago dashi infused with that same sauce. No allergen disclosure is published and no GF claim is made. Celiac diners should not assume safety and would need to call ahead (079-223-8652) to ask about the exact shoyu used — though substitution is unlikely for a bento format.
himeji_takeda_no_anago_meshi_ma.vegan_detail: The entire menu is anago (conger eel) — there are no plant-based options. The rice is cooked in anago-based dashi stock. Nothing here is vegan.
himeji_takeda_no_anago_meshi_ma.hours_raw: 09:00–20:00 daily; irregular closures follow Festa South Building schedule
himeji_takeda_no_anago_meshi_ma.notes: Maneki Foods (まねき食品) has been a Himeji institution since 1888, when they began selling anago (conger eel) sushi at Himeji Station. The company became famous for ekisoba — the station noodle combining Chinese noodles with Japanese-style dashi — now considered Himeji's soul food. A

chef_bio.background: Maneki Foods (まねき食品) has been a Himeji institution since 1888 (Meiji 21), when it began selling anago (conger eel) sushi at Himeji Station; the company is also credited with Japan's first makunouchi station bento and is famous for Himeji's ekisoba — the station noodle combining Chinese-style noodles with Japanese dashi. After more than 130 years and six generations, the 6th-generation president spent about a year and a half developing a bento that would honour that original anago-sushi tradition in a new form.
chef_bio.philosophy: The shop aims to make anago-meshi a proud souvenir of Himeji — something that can only be tasted here, prepared and served at its freshest, best state for each order.
chef_bio.specialty: Anago bento: thick live-caught conger eel white-grilled then seared and simmered briefly in a secret sauce, served over Hyogo-grown Kinumusume rice cooked in anago dashi in a special iron pot, finished with rare domestic 金播磨 sesame and stone-ground Kishu (Wakayama) grape sanshō.

anecdotes.text: The 6th-generation president spent about a year and a half developing the recipe before the August 7, 2020 opening, wanting a bento that could stand alongside — even surpass — their celebrated anago sushi rather than a typical station lunch.
The rice is cooked in a custom iron pot using dashi drawn from the anago itself, concentrating the eel's flavour into each grain.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: まねき食品公式・himeji-festa・旅色・ライブドア/オリコン報道より。まねき食品は1888年(明治21年)創業、姫路駅であなご寿司や日本初の幕の内駅弁を販売。6代目社長就任を機に約1年半かけて『たけだの穴子めし』を開発、2020年8月7日開業。活〆真穴子を白焼き後炙り秘伝だれで、兵庫県産きぬむすめを穴子だしで炊き、金播磨ごま・紀州ぶどう山椒で仕上げる。

gf_cross_contamination.text: No allergen disclosure is published. The cooking liquid and sauce contain standard Japanese soy sauce (wheat). Cross-contamination risk within the bento kitchen is unknown.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The proprietary tare used to glaze and simmer the anago is made with soy sauce; Japanese soy sauce (koikuchi) standardly contains wheat. The rice is cooked in the same anago-shoyu dashi. No GF soy sauce alternative is mentioned anywhere.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The entire product is animal-based (eel, eel dashi, shoyu). There is no plant-based item on the menu and no segregation relevant to vegan contact.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No published allergy protocol. Reservations are available and phone inquiries are possible (079-223-8652), but no allergy accommodation policy has been documented.

positives.text: Simple, focused menu of just two bento sizes means ingredient consistency is high — what you get today is what every other customer gets.

cultural_comfort.note: Counter takeout window inside a modern shopping building; ordering is straightforward but staff interaction is in Japanese.

himeji_ametuchi.gf_detail: Organic cafe run by an athlete couple. Specific rice-flour (米粉) items are gluten-free: the 有機米粉ワッフル (organic rice-flour waffle) and the 米粉キャロットケーキ, which is described on-site as グルテンフリー. The shop states it wants to offer 『小麦アレルギーの人も楽しめるメニューを』 (menus that people with wheat allergy can also enjoy). CROSS-CONTACT CAVEAT: the same kitchen bakes homemade rye bread using organic wheat 『春よ恋』(Haru-yo-koi) blended with rye — wheat flour is handled on-premises, so this is a shared kitchen, not a celiac-dedicated one. Order only the named rice-flour items and tell staff it is a coeliac child.
himeji_ametuchi.vegan_detail: Organic, additive-free focus but not a vegan kitchen — many items use egg, cheese and butter (egg-cheese toast, tomato-cheese toast, red-bean butter toast, cakes). A few plant-based items exist but vegan choices are limited; confirm each item.
himeji_ametuchi.hours_raw: 9:00–17:00 (L.O. 16:30), morning menu until 11:30. For closing days, refer to the calendar on the official Instagram/Highlights.
himeji_ametuchi.notes: [GF] Only the named rice-flour items (米粉ワッフル、米粉キャロットケーキ) are gluten-free. The bakery makes wheat/rye bread daily in the same kitchen, so flour is airborne — treat as options with real cross-contact risk. Tell staff it is coeliac (セリアック) and stick to the labelled 米粉/グルテンフリー items.

chef_bio.background: ametuchi is run by an athlete couple; one holds an international football (soccer) referee credential and has officiated at the FIFA level. They cite childhood illness as the reason for prioritising food-based health, choosing organic and additive-free ingredients sourced from across Japan. The shop relocated from Ōtsu-ku to Shikama-ku Kamo and reopened there in January 2025 after a full renovation. Coffee training was done under mentor roaster 『JOKI COFFEE』 in Kōchi, whose five specialty beans they serve.
chef_bio.philosophy: 『オーガニックをより身近に』 — make organic everyday and approachable, additive-free, including menu items that wheat-allergy customers can enjoy (note: the kitchen also bakes organic-wheat and rye bread, so it is not a dedicated gluten-free facility).
chef_bio.specialty: Specialty coffee, organic morning plates, rice-flour (米粉) waffles and cakes, alongside house-baked organic-wheat/rye bread.

anecdotes.text: Homemade almond butter is made with Kikaijima cane sugar and Yotsuba butter; European vintage dishware (Denmark Kronjørn, Finland Arabia) is used throughout.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: TANOSU取材記事・てくてくひめじ・公式サイトより。アスリート夫婦(片方はFIFA国際サッカー審判員)が営むオーガニックカフェ。2025年1月に大津区から飾磨区加茂へ移転オープン。高知『JOKI COFFEE』で焙煎を学び5種の豆を提供。米粉ワッフル・米粉キャロットケーキ(グルテンフリー)を出す一方、有機小麦『春よ恋』＋ライ麦の自家製パンも焼く(専用GF工房ではない)。

gf_cross_contamination.text: 自家製ライ麦パンは有機小麦『春よ恋』＋有機ライ麦＋天然酵母で焼いており、店内キッチンで小麦粉を扱う=共用調理環境。

vegan_cross_contact.text: 卵・チーズ・バターを使うトーストやケーキが主力で、乳・卵と同一環境。

staff_allergy_handling.text: 『小麦アレルギーの人も楽しめるメニューを』と掲げ、米粉ワッフル・米粉キャロットケーキをグルテンフリーとして提供。

positives.text: 特別栽培米の米粉と有機米油を使った米粉キャロットケーキをグルテンフリーとして明示。

himeji_cafuu.gf_detail: [Held at "ask" 2026-08-20] The description below was not traceable to any source, so the GF label is held down until it is. cafuu is a fully vegan restaurant whose retail baked goods and bread are its gluten-free strong point: the venue states plainly "焼き菓子やパン販売：12時～(allグルテンフリー)" — all baked goods and bread sold from noon are gluten-free — and the pastry chef's Instagram bio confirms items are "卵・乳・白砂糖不使用、グルテンフリー". Those bakery items are the celiac-safe zone. The reservation-only omakase lunch course is a separate matter and must be confirmed dish-by-dish: as a vegan course it can rely on wheat-derived proteins (seitan / グルテンミート / 生麩 / 車麩) for mains, and the reported course historically included a wheat "白パン" (kodama-yeast white bread), so the lunch is NOT gluten-free. Kept at "options" for this reason — bakery counter safe, lunch needs item-by-item verification with the chef when reserving.
himeji_cafuu.vegan_detail: Fully vegan (完全菜食). Vegewel and Hachidory both categorize cafuu as すべてVEGAN, the shop brands itself "vegan restaurant cafuu," and the owners note "cafuuは、作り手もヴィーガンです" (the makers are vegan too). Everything — the omakase lunch course and the counter bakery — is free of animal products, and dishes use ~50 varieties of seasonal organic, pesticide-free vegetables with completely additive-free (完全無添加) seasonings.
himeji_cafuu.hours_raw: Lunch 10:30~ (reservation required, book ~2 days in advance; one group of 2-4 per day). Baked goods & bread sales 12:00~ (all gluten-free). Café 15:00~ (roughly to 17:00). Reservation-only, one group per day; closed days not clearly published — confirm by phone 079-227-6023.
himeji_cafuu.notes: [GF] Bakery-safe, lunch-ask. The retail baked goods and bread (sold from 12:00) are the venue's own "allグルテンフリー" line and are the reliable celiac-safe choice for a 13-year-old. The reservation-only vegan omakase lunch is NOT gluten-free by default — vegan mains can use seitan/wheat gluten (グルテンミート・生麩・車麩) and the course historically included a wheat white bread — so if lunch is booked, tell them 'セリアック病・小麦アレルギー、グルテン厳禁' and confirm every dish item-by-item, or stick to the GF bakery counter. Lunch is one group of 2-4 per day and must be reserved ~2 days ahead (TEL 079-227-6023).

chef_bio.chef_name: 釣 (Tsuri) — chef; 釣真優子 (Mayuko Tsuri) — pastry chef
chef_bio.background: cafuu is run by a husband-and-wife team — chef 釣 (Tsuri, whose own Instagram @cafuu3283 gives his given name as 満也) and pastry chef 釣真優子 (Mayuko Tsuri, @momomayu321). Before Himeji the chef spent about eleven years in Okinawa — roughly six at a hotel on Ishigaki Island and five more running cafés and restaurants on the main island — where he trained in Italian, French and authentic Okinawan cooking; the name 'cafuu' (カフー) is the Okinawan word for good fortune / a treasured blessing. The couple opened cafuu in Himeji in September 2014 and relocated from the former 西今宿 location to the current 西新在家 1-1-8 address in February 2020. Each course is built around roughly 50 kinds of seasonal, pesticide-free vegetables from local (and Okinawan) farmers, prepared completely additive-free; the pastry chef runs the gluten-free vegan bakery counter (egg/dairy/white-sugar-free).
chef_bio.philosophy: To prove that『ヴィーガン＝美味しい』(vegan equals delicious) using organic, pesticide-free, completely additive-free (完全無添加) ingredients — the makers are vegan themselves.
chef_bio.specialty: Reservation-only vegan omakase course lunch; gluten-free vegan baked goods sold from the counter from noon.

However the baked sweets (financiers, cookies, florentines) and all decoration cakes/tarts contain egg and dairy, and several savoury breads (塩バターパン, ウィンナーロール, 厚焼き玉子サンド) contain butter, sausage or egg — so the shop is not fully vegan.
himeji_milbake.hours_raw: Irregular — check open days on the official Instagram (sells out and closes when products run out). Bread days ~11:00–15:00; cake pickup days ~12:00–15:00. Solo operator; days vary week to week.
himeji_milbake.notes: [GF-dedicated] A solo, wheat-free rice-flour workshop — the owner uses no wheat flour on the premises, so celiac cross-contact from flour is essentially nil. Breads are 米粉100% and vegan-friendly; sweets and cakes contain egg/dairy but are still gluten-free. Hours are irregular and stock sells out, so check the Instagram (@mil.bakeshop) and reserve/DM before travelling; cash only, ~2.5 km west of Himeji Castle with only 2 parking spaces.

chef_bio.background: MIL bake is run single-handedly by its owner, a trained pâtissier who developed an occupational wheat allergy while working with flour — she reports asthma, runny nose (rhinitis), hand dermatitis and itchy eyes on contact with wheat, on top of pre-existing allergic rhinitis and fatigue. Forced away from conventional patisserie, she discovered rice flour (米粉) and rebuilt her craft around it, opening MIL bake as a wheat-free workshop where 「工房では小麦粉を使用しません」. The shop relocated and reopened at its current 田寺 (Tadera 8-13-52) address on September 28, 2025, having previously operated from a smaller home workshop (御立中) with weekly Instagram-announced sales. She runs everything herself, taking orders via LINE and Instagram DM and warning replies may be slow.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「国産米粉となるべく身体に負担のない材料で」— to bake with domestic rice flour and ingredients as gentle on the body as possible, and to make gluten-free food that everyone, allergic or not, finds genuinely delicious, so that 米粉 products become a normal sight on shelves.
chef_bio.specialty: 米粉100% breads (山食パン loaf, baguette, rolls) plus rice-flour baked sweets and made-to-order decoration cakes and tarts. Breads are made without wheat, dairy, egg or nuts.

anecdotes.text: As wheat allergies increase, the owner says she wants to offer 「グルテンフリーでも誰もが楽しめる美味しい食べ物」 — gluten-free food everyone can enjoy — not just something for the allergic.
The shop states it was created for 「小麦アレルギー、小麦不耐性、小麦をドクターストップされている方々」 — people with wheat allergy, wheat intolerance, or under doctor's orders to avoid wheat.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式(crayonsite)・local-prime・tanosu・budou-chanより。店主は元パティシエで、小麦により喘息・鼻水・手湿疹・目の痒みを発症し米粉専門工房を開業。「工房では小麦粉を使用しません」「米粉100%」「小麦・乳・卵・ナッツ不使用(パン)」を明言。2025年9月28日、田寺8-13-52へ移転リニューアル。店主個人名はいずれの媒体にも未掲載。

gf_cross_contamination.text: 「工房では小麦粉を使用しません」— no wheat flour is used anywhere in the workshop, so flour cross-contact is not a factor.
All bread is described as 米粉100%; breads are 「小麦・乳・卵・ナッツ不使用」 per the shop.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Bakery — no soy sauce in products. 豆乳ロールパン contains soy milk (not soy sauce); soy-sensitive guests should note it.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Egg and dairy are used in the same wheat-free workshop for sweets and cakes; vegans should stick to the plain 米粉 breads listed as egg/dairy-free.

staff_allergy_handling.text: Owner is herself a wheat-allergic former pâtissier who built the shop specifically for wheat allergy / intolerance / medically wheat-restricted customers; fruit allergies and preferences accommodated on request.

positives.text: Entirely wheat-free rice-flour workshop run by an allergy-affected owner — 「なるべく身体に負担のない材料で」, using domestic rice flour, potato starch, rice oil, beet sugar and sea salt.
Breads free of wheat, dairy, egg and nuts — usable by celiac and vegan guests alike.

owner_signoff.reason: Greg, applying the amended evidence bar. Own facility claim 「工房では小麦粉を使用しません」 plus four independent first-hand visits (Kiss PRESS sampled and interviewed the owner; local-prime bylined editorial visit; tanosu journalist visit with original photography recording 「小麦・乳・卵・ナッツ不使用」; 姫路の種 photographed in person). The owner is a former patissier with occupational wheat allergy / 小麦粉喘息 and physically cannot handle wheat — a structural guarantee stronger than most written protocols. Absence from English-language celiac platforms is not a disqualifier.

gf_review.why: I tried to find wheat anywhere in this operation and failed — the shop's own site states plainly 「工房では小麦粉を使用しません」 and 「国産米粉となるべく身体に負担のない材料で」, and the owner's motive is unusually credible: multiple independent reporters who interviewed her in person confirm she is a former pâtissier who developed occupational wheat allergy/小麦粉喘息 and can no longer handle wheat at all. Corroboration here is genuinely independent and first-hand: Kiss PRESS's reporter visited, sampled and interviewed the owner; local-prime.com ran a bylined editorial visit; tanosu.com ran a journalist visit with original photography noting the breads are 「小麦・乳・卵・ナッツ不使用」; and the 姫路の種 blogger photographed the storefront in person. What blocks `dedicated` is the protocol's other requirement — I found no celiac-grade corroboration at all (no FindMeGlutenFree or HappyCow entry, no GF-Japan list; the FMGF Himeji results surface other shops entirely), so the dedicated bar is not met and it drops one rung. Note also that the record's own-site evidence describes a home workshop, while the shop has since moved to a retail storefront in 田寺 (28 Sept 2025) and dropped its reservation-only model.
red_flags: No celiac-grade corroboration found (no FindMeGlutenFree, no HappyCow, no GF-Japan list entry) — fails the dedicated bar even though independent local reporting is strong
No source states an explicit cross-contamination or dedicated-equipment protocol; the wheat-free conclusion rests on the owner's medical inability to handle wheat plus a rice-flour-only product line
Record's cited local-prime and couleur-harima pages still list the OLD address 姫路市御立中2-5-20; the shop relocated to 姫路市田寺8-13-52 S-4 on 28 Sept 2025

Hours are irregular and posted only via Instagram; the shop closes when sold out

gf_review.plain_rice: No — rice-flour bakery, no cooked-rice dishes. Not a plain-gohan option.
gf_review.identity_note: Identity confirmed and open: MIL bake※ 米粉専門店, 兵庫県姫路市田寺8丁目13-52 S-4 (opposite Shimamura Tadera), relocated/reopened 28 Sept 2025, Instagram @mil.bakeshop, site milbake.crayonsite.info. The record's 田寺 neighborhood is current; several of its cited sources predate the move and give the old 御立中 address, and the record's 'home workshop, reservation-only' framing is out of date — walk-ins are now accepted.

himeji_reborn_curry.gf_detail: [Held at "ask" 2026-08-20] The description below was not traceable to any source, so the GF label is held down until it is. [Adversarial GF review 2026-08-19: high→options. This was the scrutiny target and the label breaks on the shop's own menu. The official HotPepper menu carries the line 「サモサは揚げ餃子風です。サモサ以外グルテンフリーです。」 — 'the samosa is fried-gyoza style; everything EXCEPT the samosa is gluten-free' — i.e. the shop itself confirms wheat gyoza wrappers are deep-fried in its kitchen, and tanosu independently reports the samosa is made with 餃子の皮. The side menu also lists タンドリーチキン唐揚げ and パコラ, both deep-fried, with no dedicated fryer or separate-oil claim from any source, and the flagship ¥1,870 Reborn Obanzai lunch (10/day) puts that same karaage on the plate alongside the curry — so a celiac ordering the headline lunch set eats out of the shared fryer. Every 'gluten-free' citation traces back to one origin: the shop's own marketing, echoed by four local Himeji promo outlets (KissPress, tanosu, budou-chan, keizai.biz) covering the May 2024 opening; there is no celiac-grade source, no FindMeGlutenFree/HappyCow entry, and no allergen protocol. The shop's own 「グレインフリー」 (grain-free) wording for a curry served over rice further shows the terminology is marketing, not allergen rigour.] This spice-curry specialist markets every curry as wheat-free: the official site says 「グレインフリーのカレーをご堪能下さい」(enjoy our grain-free curry) and the KissPress review confirms 「同店のカレーは全てグルテンフリー」(all of the shop's curries are gluten-free), also noting the curries are butter-free (バター不使用). The base is rice with a house blend of 15 spices, so the curry plates themselves should contain no wheat. HOWEVER this is a SHARED (not dedicated) kitchen and the menu also includes samosa / keema-samosa (サモサ / キーマサモサ) whose pastry is traditionally wheat flour, so wheat is handled on premises — cross-contact is possible and a celiac should stick to the curry plates, skip the samosa, and confirm the day's spice blend and any garnish contain no wheat.
himeji_reborn_curry.vegan_detail: The mains are all animal-based — bone-in chicken curries, meat keema, and boiled egg — and the lassi and cheesecake are dairy, so there is no vegan main. A few plant sides exist (野菜のスパイス炒め vegetable spice stir-fry, スパイスポテト spiced potatoes, アチャール pickles) and black coffee, which may be vegan but are not confirmed as animal-free by the shop. A vegan diner would need to ask and cobble together sides.
himeji_reborn_curry.hours_raw: Mon–Tue & Fri–Sun 11:00–15:00 and 17:00–21:00 (curry L.O. 14:30 / 20:30, café 15:00–17:00); Thu 11:00–15:00 lunch only; closed Wednesdays
himeji_reborn_curry.notes: [GF] Spice-curry specialist that brands all of its curries as gluten-free / grain-free and butter-free — a strong fit for a celiac, and there is a kids' curry (キッズカレー) making it workable for a 13-year-old. This is NOT a dedicated GF kitchen: samosa (wheat pastry) is on the menu, so avoid it and ask staff to keep the curry plate away from any floured items. Rice-based plates with a 15-spice house blend; confirm the blend and any garnishes are wheat-free on the day. Closed Wednesdays; Thursday is lunch only.

chef_bio.chef_name: 森岩大和 (Moriishi Yamato) — surname appears as 森石 in some coverage
chef_bio.background: Reborn Curry opened on May 1, 2024 in the Okada district of Himeji (a first-floor unit), operated by GP&M (ジーピーエム), an amusement-equipment company for which this is a first venture into food service (Himeji Keizai Shimbun). The manager — given as 森岩大和 (Moriishi Yamato) by Himeji Keizai and 森石 (Moriishi) by KissPress — is described as passionate about both music and curry. As a university student in Matsumoto, Nagano he became a devoted regular of an Indian restaurant called シュプラ (Shupra), since closed; he set out to 'reborn' those flavours, which is the source of the shop's name. The venue doubles as a record café where guests can request vinyl.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「専門店のカレーとコーヒーで元気（パワー）を提供する」— to recharge customers' energy through specialty curry and coffee; the curries are cooked gluten-free and butter-free (as advertised by the shop) so the stomach stays light.
chef_bio.specialty: Rice-based spice curry using a 15-spice house blend — a signature dry keema (with peas and pickle) paired with a soupier chicken curry, plus a bone-in chicken curry slow-simmered until the skin turns tender and gelatinous.

anecdotes.text: The shop is named 'Reborn' because the owner set out to revive the flavours of シュプラ (Shupra), a now-closed Indian restaurant in Matsumoto, Nagano, that he loved as a student.
It is a record café: vinyl lines the walls and customers can request songs or bring their own records; 80s hits were playing during one reviewer's visit.
The operator, GP&M, is an amusement-equipment company entering food service for the first time.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Shared (not dedicated GF) kitchen; samosa / keema-samosa on the menu use traditionally wheat-flour pastry, so wheat is present on premises and cross-contact is possible — celiac guests should avoid the samosa and confirm plating.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Curries use a 15-spice house blend; commercial garam-masala / curry-powder blends are occasionally cut with wheat flour, so the specific blend should be confirmed wheat-free on the day.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: No soy sauce is mentioned in the curry recipes; South-Asian-style spice curry typically uses none, but this is not explicitly confirmed — ask whether any しょうゆ/soy sauce is used and, if so, whether it is tamari.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Mains are chicken/keema/egg based and desserts/lassi are dairy; plant sides are not confirmed animal-free, so vegans must ask.

staff_allergy_handling.text: The shop actively advertises its curries as gluten-free / grain-free and butter-free, indicating awareness of wheat-avoidance, but no formal allergen protocol or dedicated-kitchen claim is documented.

himeji_retreat_field.gf_detail: Welfare-run farm (就労継続支援B型) in northern Himeji that direct-sells rice-flour snacks and noodles made from its own naturally-cultivated rice — 『自然栽培農法で育てたお米や、その米粉を使った米粉麺』. The rice-flour dried noodles are marketed as gluten-free so 『小麦アレルギーの人でも食べられる』, and the signature snack 『ぽりっと』 (potato + rice flour) won bronze at the 2022 授産品コンクール. These are single-ingredient-transparent rice products, but this is a small production/直売 facility, not a certified gluten-free line — confirm the specific product and that it is not made on a shared wheat line. Note it is primarily a shop/直売所; hot food only at the monthly はたけカフェ.
himeji_retreat_field.vegan_detail: The rice-flour snacks (ぽりっと) and dried rice noodles are plant-based; the seasonal プリン (pudding) likely contains egg/dairy. Vegan is item-by-item — confirm.
himeji_retreat_field.hours_raw: Farm-stand sales 10:00–17:00, closed Sat, Sun & holidays. The Hatake Cafe (lunch set) is held once a month. Online sales via BASE (makinorf.thebase.in). Parking available. 7 min by car from Funatsu IC.
