himeji_retreat_field.notes: [GF] A direct-sales shop, not a restaurant — buy the rice-flour 米粉乾燥麺 and ぽりっと snack (naturally-cultivated rice, marketed GF) or order online via BASE. Weekends and holidays are closed; hot meals only at the once-a-month はたけカフェ. Confirm the production line is not shared with wheat before buying for a coeliac child.

chef_bio.background: Retreat Field is operated by NPO法人 姫路こころの事業団 as a Type-B continuous employment support workplace (就労継続支援B型事業所) in Yamada-chō Makino (山田町牧野619-1), northern Himeji. It grows rice and vegetables by natural cultivation (no pesticide or chemical fertiliser) and develops rice-flour products so that people with wheat allergy can eat them. Its potato-and-rice-flour snack 『ぽりっと』 won a bronze prize at the 2022 はばたけ授産品コンクール, and it has developed chewy rice-flour dried noodles that cook in about 1.5–2 minutes. Products are sold on-site and online via BASE, with a monthly はたけカフェ.
chef_bio.philosophy: Provide meaningful work on a natural-cultivation farm while making gluten-free rice-flour food that wheat-allergic people can enjoy.
chef_bio.specialty: Naturally-cultivated rice, chewy rice-flour dried noodles, the ぽりっと potato-rice-flour snack, and seasonal veg/fruit puddings.

anecdotes.text: 『ぽりっと』ははばたけ授産品コンクール2022で銅賞を受賞。もちもち食感の米粉乾燥麺(調理約1.5〜2分)も開発した。

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 姫路みたい特集・神戸新聞(Yahoo!転載)・BASE通販より。NPO法人姫路こころの事業団が運営する就労継続支援B型の農園(山田町牧野619-1)。自然栽培米の米粉を使ったグルテンフリー菓子『ぽりっと』(2022はばたけ授産品コンクール銅賞)や米粉乾燥麺を直売/通販。月1回はたけカフェ開催。

gf_cross_contamination.text: 小規模な就労施設の製造・直売所。米粉製品専用ラインか小麦と共用かは未確認。要確認。

vegan_cross_contact.text: 季節のプリンは卵・乳を含む可能性。ぽりっと・米粉麺は植物性。

staff_allergy_handling.text: 『自然栽培農法で育てたお米や、その米粉を使った米粉麺』を販売。米粉麺は小麦アレルギーの人でも食べられるとする。

positives.text: 自然栽培米100%の米粉を使ったグルテンフリーの菓子・乾燥麺。ぽりっとは授産品コンクール銅賞。

himeji_sai_cafe.gf_detail: Fully vegan cafe on the north side of Himeji Castle. The packaged baked sweets (produced by 岡山『いぶき』/Ibuki) are the confirmed gluten-free line: donuts, cookies, madeleines, lemon cake and snowballs, all 『動物性原材料不使用且つ8大アレルゲンフリー』(no animal ingredients and free of the 8 major allergens — which includes wheat), made with rice flour instead of wheat. CAVEAT: the signature 斎麺 (sai-men vegetable ramen: ginger / ashitaba / chlorella noodles) has NO published gluten-free claim and ramen noodles are normally wheat — treat hot food as not verified GF. Craft beer (barley) is also served on premises. Stick to the 8-allergen-free Ibuki sweets and confirm any savoury dish directly.
himeji_sai_cafe.vegan_detail: Entirely plant-based. The shop states its menu uses 『動物性原材料、精製糖、うまみ調味料、アルコール調味料、乳製品は使わない』 (no animal ingredients, refined sugar, MSG, alcohol seasonings or dairy). Recipes are supervised by Tokyo vegan restaurant 菜道 (Saido), rated among the world's best. Vegan beer available too.
himeji_sai_cafe.hours_raw: 11:00–17:00 (food L.O. 16:00 / drink & sweets L.O. 16:30). Temporarily closed from around December 2025 for a menu renewal, reopening planned for spring 2026. The official site posts normal business hours. Before visiting, confirm the operating status on the official Instagram (@saicafe__himeji).
himeji_sai_cafe.notes: [GF] Vegan cafe; confirmed GF items are the Ibuki packaged sweets (8-major-allergen-free, rice flour). The house 斎麺 ramen noodles carry no GF claim and are presumed wheat, and barley craft beer is served, so this is an options venue for a coeliac, not a safe hot-meal choice. IMPORTANT: was temporarily closed for a menu renewal until spring 2026 — verify it has reopened via Instagram before travelling.

chef_bio.background: Owner Yano Eitarō previously ran an izakaya in Himeji. Recognising that Himeji Castle draws many international visitors yet the city lacked vegetarian/vegan dining, and after encountering chef Kusumoto Katsushige (楠本勝三) of the Tokyo vegan restaurant 菜道 (Saido), he opened SAI CAFE on March 21, 2023 (白国北新町). The recipes are supervised by Saido, widely reported as a 'world's best vegan restaurant'. The name 『SAI』 layers 菜 (vegetables), the signature 斎麺, 菜道 (the mentoring restaurant) and サイ (rhinoceros).
chef_bio.philosophy: Deliver satisfying yet fully plant-based food — no animal products, refined sugar, MSG, alcohol seasoning or dairy — so health-conscious and international diners can enjoy it.
chef_bio.specialty: 斎麺 (a vividly coloured, all-vegetable ramen offered with a choice of noodle types), vegetable curry, vegan sweets and specialty coffee; sweets are made by Okayama's Ibuki (いぶき), animal-free and 8-major-allergen-free.

anecdotes.text: 菜道シェフ楠本勝三氏との出会いがきっかけで開業、レシピは菜道が監修。
The vegan, 8-major-allergen-free sweet line (donuts, cookies, madeleines, lemon cake, snowballs) is produced by Okayama-based Ibuki with no animal ingredients and no artificial colours.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 姫路経済新聞・Kiss PRESS・Food Diversity・公式サイトより。元居酒屋店主の矢野英太郎氏が2023年3月21日に白国北新町で開業。東京の菜道(楠本勝三シェフ)が監修する完全ヴィーガン店。看板の斎麺は野菜で作った色鮮やかな麺。菓子は岡山いぶき製で動物性不使用＋8大アレルゲンフリー。店名は菜・斎麺・菜道・サイ(犀)に由来(公式)。

gf_cross_contamination.text: 斎麺(ラーメン)の麺にグルテンフリー表記なし=通常小麦麺の想定。焼き菓子(いぶき製)は8大アレルゲンフリーだが提供環境は要確認。
店内でクラフトビール(Free Spirits Brewing／大麦)を提供。

vegan_cross_contact.text: 完全ヴィーガン。動物性原材料・乳製品・精製糖・うまみ調味料・アルコール調味料は不使用。

staff_allergy_handling.text: 『動物性原材料不使用且つ8大アレルゲンフリーだけでなく、着色料や添加物も不使用で安心・安全の商品』としてヴィーガン菓子を販売。

positives.text: ドーナツ・クッキー・マドレーヌ・レモンケーキ・スノーボールは動物性不使用＋8大アレルゲンフリー(小麦不使用・米粉)。

himeji_sangohachi.gf_detail: Organic natural-food cafe/restaurant one minute from JR Gochaku station. The kitchen uses homemade organic koji (麹) seasonings and states 『調理にはなるべく小麦粉や砂糖を使っていない』 (they avoid using wheat flour and sugar as much as possible), so many plates are flour-free — e.g. the バターナッツかぼちゃのハンバーグ is made 『小麦粉を使わず』 (without wheat flour). BUT wheat is not eliminated: 小麦粉は一部メニューのみ使用 (wheat is used in some items), toast is on the menu, and notably the signature pound cake is 『九州産の自然栽培の大麦粉を100%使用』 (100% barley flour = gluten). This is a negotiable, ask-first venue: request a wheat-free plate and confirm the soy sauce/miso used with the koji seasonings. Not a coeliac-dedicated kitchen.
himeji_sangohachi.vegan_detail: Offers explicit vegan choices such as the バターナッツかぼちゃのハンバーグ弁当 (labelled 'for vegan'). Uses organic eggs and dairy elsewhere, so vegan is item-by-item — ask.
himeji_sangohachi.hours_raw: Tue–Fri 11:30–22:00 (L.O. 21:00) / Sat 9:00–22:00 (L.O. 21:00) / Sun & holidays 9:00–17:00 (L.O. 16:00). Morning menu by reservation only, Sat/Sun/holidays 9:00–10:30. Closed Mon (if a holiday, open 9:00–17:00 and closed the following Tue).

himeji_sangohachi.notes: [GF] Ask-first. Much of the cooking is deliberately wheat-flour-free and built on homemade koji, and staff can prepare a flour-free plate — but wheat is still used in some dishes, toast is served, and the house pound cake is 100% barley flour (gluten). For a coeliac child, phone ahead, explain セリアック, ask for a 小麦粉不使用 plate and confirm the soy sauce/miso is wheat-free (barley miso is common).

chef_bio.background: Owner Kaizuka Akiko developed an interest in organic food as a student after struggling with atopy, chemical sensitivity and hay fever, which led her to limit everything she puts into her body to organic and additive-free ingredients. She opened 珊瑚椀 around 2019 near JR Gochaku station (御国野町御着), marking a third anniversary in 2022, and built the concept around homemade organic koji seasonings — dubbing the style 『オーガニックジャンキー』 (organic junk food that is nonetheless clean). All ingredients are organic/pesticide-free with no additives or chemical seasonings.
chef_bio.philosophy: Serve satisfying 'organic junkie' comfort food using only organic, additive-free ingredients and homemade koji seasonings; minimise wheat flour and sugar.
chef_bio.specialty: Weekly-changing organic lunch, koji-seasoned dishes, butternut-squash koji hamburg (vegan version), 100% barley-flour pound cake.

anecdotes.text: アトピー・化学物質過敏症・花粉症の経験から、体に入れる食材・調味料を有機・無添加に限定した店を構えた。

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 姫路経済新聞(3周年記事)・TANOSU取材・公式サイトより。店主貝塚暁子さんが2019年開業(2022年8月8日で3周年)。自家製麹調味料＋有機食材の『オーガニックジャンキー』。小麦粉・砂糖はなるべく不使用、スイーツは大麦粉・グルテンフリー、パウンドケーキは九州産大麦粉100%。

gf_cross_contamination.text: 小麦粉は一部メニューのみ使用、トーストも提供＝共用調理環境。要相談。

soy_sauce_wheat.text: 自家製麹調味料は有機だが、醤油・味噌の小麦・大麦有無は未確認。要確認。

vegan_cross_contact.text: 有機卵・乳を使うメニューもあり、ヴィーガンは要指定。

staff_allergy_handling.text: 『調理にはなるべく小麦粉や砂糖を使っていない』。バターナッツかぼちゃのハンバーグは小麦粉不使用で作れる。

positives.text: 有機・無添加・無農薬食材のみ使用、自家製麹調味料はグルテンフリー。多くの料理が小麦粉不使用。

himeji_satonaka.gf_detail: [Held at "ask" 2026-08-20] The description below was not traceable to any source, so the GF label is held down until it is. The venue's own words: 「無添加・無化調・小麦粉不使用グルテンフリーのスパイスチキンカレー」 and 「すべてのカレーが小麦粉不使用なのでアレルギー持ちの人も安心」 — every curry sauce is made with no wheat flour, thickened by an 8-spice blend and an additive-free dashi of kombu, shiitake and chicken bones simmered daily, served over turmeric rice. However this is a SHARED (not dedicated) kitchen that also cooks wheat: the chicken katsu curry and the chicken-cutlet topping are panko-breaded and fried, and the Himeji branch also serves keema curry pasta and cheese curry doria. Because breaded/fried wheat items and pasta are prepared in the same space, the wheat-free curries are best treated as GF options with real cross-contact risk rather than a fully gluten-free venue — order a plain curry (no katsu, no seasoned egg), confirm the topping and any seasoning, and flag the celiac requirement.
himeji_satonaka.vegan_detail: There is no vegan main: the curry dashi is built on chicken bones (鶏ガラ) and the curries contain chicken. Only side/topping items lean plant-based — the cabbage pickles (ピクルス ¥100) and the potato sabzi that accompanies the keema are vegetable-based, while the lassi and cheese are dairy. A vegan diner could not make a meal here beyond sides.
himeji_satonaka.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 11:30–15:00 (L.O. 14:30) & 17:30–20:00 (L.O. 19:30); Sun 11:30–15:00 lunch only; closed 1st & 3rd Mondays
himeji_satonaka.notes: [GF] Every curry sauce here is genuinely made without wheat flour — the shop advertises 「小麦粉不使用グルテンフリーのスパイスチキンカレー」 and it is a good, mild, kid-friendly curry-and-rice (turmeric rice) for a celiac 13-year-old. But it is a shared kitchen that also fries panko chicken katsu and cooks pasta and doria, so avoid the katsu curry, the chicken-cutlet topping and the seasoned soft-boiled egg (soy-based marinade), order a plain chicken or mushroom-chicken curry, and clearly state the wheat allergy so staff plate it away from the fried/breaded items.

chef_bio.background: Motomachi Satonaka is a noren-wake (independent spin-off) of the original 'Satonaka' curry shop in Sannomiya, Kobe. The Motomachi flagship opened in 2014 about five minutes north of JR Motomachi Station, after its owner tasted the original Satonaka curry, was moved to declare 「このカレーをつくりたい！」 ('I want to make this curry!'), and trained until he could reproduce the recipe 'down to the gram.' The Himeji branch opened on 19 February 2023 as the group's second location, run by a store manager named Ichii (一井) who trained at the Motomachi shop. The brand has since expanded to Takasago and Suzurandai branches as well.
chef_bio.philosophy: Additive-free and no chemical seasonings ('無添加・無化調'), gluten-free and 'body-friendly' (からだにやさしい) — wheat flour is never used to thicken the curry; umami comes instead from a slow dashi of kombu, shiitake and chicken bones simmered about three hours daily.
chef_bio.specialty: Wheat-free spice curry built on an 8-spice blend (cardamom, cumin, clove and others) and chicken-bone/kombu/shiitake dashi, served over turmeric rice; domestic chicken breast is defatted and cooked separately at low temperature.

anecdotes.text: The owner was so struck by the original Sannomiya Satonaka curry that he resolved 「このカレーをつくりたい！」 and trained to master the recipe by the gram.
The Himeji branch's store manager, Ichii, trained at the original Motomachi location before opening the Himeji shop on 19 February 2023.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Japanese sources (tanosu 167317, kisspress 39742, brand site) consistently describe Satonaka as an additive-free, no-chemical-seasoning, gluten-free spice-curry shop whose curries use no wheat flour, thickened instead by a ~3hr kombu/shiitake/chicken-bone dashi; they attribute the shop to an owner who spun off from the Sannomiya original in 2014 and give the Himeji manager's name as Ichii (一井), but no single named founder/chef is published.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Shared kitchen: the chicken katsu curry and chicken-cutlet topping are panko-breaded and fried, and the Himeji branch also serves keema curry pasta and cheese curry doria — all wheat items cooked in the same space as the wheat-free curries, so cross-contact is possible.
gf_cross_contamination.why: The katsu half is supported (チキンカツカレー plus a ¥310 チキンカツ topping), but there is NO keema curry pasta and NO cheese curry doria on this menu page — 0 hits for パスタ, and the only ドリア is a stray Tabelog keyword-cloud tag. The 12-item menu is six curries plus six toppings. Remove the pasta/doria detail; t

gf_cross_contamination.text: The shop's claim is specifically that the curries use no wheat flour ('すべてのカレーが小麦粉不使用'), not that the whole kitchen is gluten-free; no dedicated GF prep line or fryer is mentioned in any source.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: No Japanese source mentions soy sauce (醤油) or tamari in the curry; the base is described as an additive-free dashi of kombu, shiitake and chicken bones, so the curry sauce itself appears free of soy sauce.
Caveat: the 半熟味付玉子 (seasoned soft-boiled egg) topping is a marinated egg that in Japan is typically steeped in a soy-sauce-based liquid (soy sauce usually contains wheat) — confirm before adding it.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Every curry contains chicken and a chicken-bone dashi, so vegan diners are limited to vegetable sides (pickles, potato sabzi); no vegan curry exists.

staff_allergy_handling.text: The shop markets its curry to allergy sufferers ('アレルギー持ちの人も安心'), indicating allergy awareness, but no source describes a specific cross-contact protocol for the shared kitchen.

positives.text: Every curry sauce is genuinely made without wheat flour ('無添加・無化調・小麦粉不使用グルテンフリーのスパイスチキンカレー'); thickening comes from an 8-spice blend and dashi, not roux.
Additive-free, no chemical seasonings, with a mild kid-friendly chicken curry over turmeric rice — a workable safe meal for a celiac child if ordered plain.

himeji_ureshinaru.gf_detail: [Held at "ask" 2026-08-20] The description below was not traceable to any source, so the GF label is held down until it is. Allergy-friendly wagashi/Western sweets cafe (opened June 2018). Its house cake sponges are all rice flour with 『卵・乳・小麦不使用』 (no egg, dairy or wheat), and made-to-order allergy cakes are offered, so genuine rice-flour gluten-free cakes exist here. CAVEAT: it is a made-to-order shop with 'anything-goes' fillings (『中身も変幻自在』) where グルテンフリー is just one of many options, and NOT every item is wheat-free — e.g. one signature cake is 『くるみ醤油と多良間黒糖 生麩仕立て』, and 生麩 (nama-fu) is wheat gluten and くるみ醤油 is wheat soy sauce. Confirm each specific cake, and note this is a small non-dedicated kitchen (cross-contact possible). For a coeliac, order only the explicitly 米粉/グルテンフリー cakes and say it is for a child.
himeji_ureshinaru.vegan_detail: The allergy line is 卵・乳・小麦不使用 (no egg/dairy/wheat) so several cakes are effectively vegan, but other variations use 生クリーム (dairy cream) and chocolate. Vegan is item-by-item — confirm.
himeji_ureshinaru.hours_raw: 11:00–17:00 (some sources say Fri until 16:30). Closed Tue & Sun (per Hitosara). Note: business days/hours differ between sources — confirm by phone. Made-to-order cakes require reservation.
himeji_ureshinaru.gmaps: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=坂の上の嬉しなる%20飾東町豊国%20姫路市%20Japan
himeji_ureshinaru.notes: [GF] Rice-flour sponge sweets shop with real gluten-free cakes, but it is made-to-order and not everything is wheat-free (one signature cake uses 生麩/wheat gluten and walnut soy sauce). Treat as options: order only the labelled 米粉/グルテンフリー cakes, ask about the specific filling, and note the small shared kitchen. Best to phone ahead (079-229-2277) and ask for a coeliac-safe custom cake.

chef_bio.background: Owner Nagai (長井さん) opened 坂の上の嬉しなる in June 2018, renovating a storage building on the family home into a small sweets cafe. The shop name 『嬉しなる』 incorporates a character from the owner's mother's name, and the owner self-roasts hojicha as a tribute to childhood memories of a mother making hojicha-yu (roasted-tea porridge). Alongside regular cakes made with domestic wheat flour, butter and eggs, the shop offers an allergy line built on rice-flour sponge that is egg-, dairy- and wheat-free (such as the 『米よし』/Komeyoshi cake, which is also soy-free), and takes fully made-to-order character/allergy cakes on advance order.
chef_bio.philosophy: Make sweets that families — including those with wheat, egg or dairy allergies — can enjoy together, combining Japanese ingredients (koji, miso, hojicha, amazake) with rice-flour sponge.
chef_bio.specialty: Rice-flour allergy cakes (egg/dairy/wheat-free), self-roasted-hojicha and amazake wagashi-Western hybrids, made-to-order character cakes.
